title: Migration Incident Review and Q4 Roadmap Sync
decisions: Schema migrations on tables with more than 10 million rows must set a lock timeout (enforced in CI), get a platform-team review, and run outside peak hours (before 8 AM or after 7 PM Eastern).
Q4 SSO scope is SAML with Okta as the first identity provider, Enterprise plan only, with a beta around November 16; Azure AD and SCIM move to Q1.

Run the usage-based pricing experiment on 10% of new self-serve signups ($29/month platform fee plus $2 per 10,000 events) for eight weeks starting October 20, billed via Stripe metered billing; existing customers are not affected.
The mobile app is not sunset this year; it goes into maintenance mode (security and OS compatibility fixes only, no new features) and is revisited in Q2.
On-call moves to half-week shifts (Monday to Thursday, Thursday to Monday) with a formal secondary and 15-minute escalation, starting October 5.
Northwind Freight gets a one-month goodwill credit (about $52,000) on its next invoice, framed as goodwill rather than an SLA credit.

actionItems.task: Write and publish the internal incident postmortem on Confluence, plus a short customer-facing version, by Thursday October 1
Add a CI lint check to the migration pipeline that fails the build when a migration does not set a lock timeout, by October 9
Set up an Okta developer tenant, spike the SAML library, and share a short writeup by Friday
Write the pricing experiment one-pager (pricing, success metrics, spending cap) by October 9
Set up the new on-call schedule in PagerDuty with primary and secondary layers and 15-minute escalation, removing Dan from November 9, live before October 5
Call Diane Walsh at Northwind on Thursday to walk through the incident, offer the credit, and confirm the mobile app is staying
Get the Northwind goodwill credit signed off by Anna in finance by Wednesday
Update the Q4 roadmap doc with today's decisions (Northwind in its own section) and share it with the leadership team by Friday
Update the outdated status page runbook (still references Statuspage instead of Instatus) so the first status post goes out within 10 minutes of an incident being declared

notDecided: Moving the events table off the main Postgres cluster (partitioning, Aurora, or Timescale); parked until Q1 planning
A change freeze for the last two weeks of December; to be revisited in November

reversed.initial: Sunset the mobile app: announce in October, pull it from the app stores, and shut it down on December 31
reversed.final: Keep the mobile app in maintenance mode (security and compatibility fixes only) with no sunset this year and revisit in Q2, because about 1,200 Northwind drivers depend on it
